subtype: Approach: visiting first to assess neighbourhoods [Action]
passage: Before I signed anything in Pune, I took a Friday off and went there for the weekend. My listings had promised "ten minutes to the office" in three different places. So at half past five, the worst hour, I rode the route from the office to each address, and each time the ten minutes turned into forty. On Saturday I walked three areas end to end: the lane behind the market, the quiet colony with the tree-lined road, the new towers near the highway. I bought tea at a stall in each and asked the vendor what the place was like at night. One was loud, one had no shops, one felt right. My wife Ishita, on the phone, asked, "And the photos?" I said, "The photos didn't show the traffic." I signed for the third area on Sunday. - Kiran

qa.q: How many areas did Kiran walk through?
How did Kiran feel about the listings after the visit?
qa.a: Kiran became sceptical and wary of them, since the promised ten minutes turned into forty.

qa.q: What else could Kiran do before signing a lease?
qa.a: Kiran could ask people who live nearby or a colleague about costs and problems, or rent short-term first, to add more direct information.

qa.q: How might Ishita have felt hearing about the trip on the phone?
qa.a: Ishita may have felt reassured and curious, wanting a real picture of the area beyond the photos.

grounding: Kiran spends a weekend in the new city, tests peak-hour commutes and visits three areas before signing a lease.
